cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_pca_warhurst_signers_2020: ZERO confirmed overlap. Warhurst is conservative complementarian PCA pastors; CBE is the ideological opposite. No names in common.
cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_pca_amr_leadership_2026: ZERO confirmed overlap among published AMR leadership names (Cassidy, Swett, Jun, Gordon, Whitfield, St. Clair, Richter, Khandjian, Keller, Radney, Ziegler, Nelson, Choi, Twit, Wells, Lucas, Cortese). AMR's soft-egalitarian leanings on women-in-leadership do not extend to formal CBE involvement. Tim Keller publicly affirmed female deacons but maintained complementarian eldership and is not on any CBE roster.
cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_pca_letter_of_lament_2025: ZERO direct overlap with published Lament signers. The Lament letter focuses on racial justice/complementarian-soft-progressives within PCA, not gender egalitarianism per se.
cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_revoice_speakers_and_endorsers: ZERO direct overlap with the 60-name Revoice list. Revoice is a Side B sexuality conference; CBE is gender egalitarian. Different theological lanes (some demographic/sociological adjacency among progressive evangelicals but no shared formal speakers).
cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_dallas_statement_signers_2018: ZERO overlap (sanity check). Dallas Statement is anti-social-justice and gender-complementarian; CBE figures would never sign it.
cross_list_overlap_analysis.with_nashville_statement_signers_2017: ZERO overlap. Aimee Byrd is the canonical test case: CBE-adjacent, did NOT sign Nashville. Beth Allison Barr also did not sign. Confirmed expected polarity.

notable_pastoral_drift_signals: No CBE leader has ever been a Nashville/Dallas signer (per documented public lists). The egalitarian/complementarian boundary remains rigid; movement across is rare.
Wade Burleson (2007 Priscilla and Aquila Award) is notable as a former Southern Baptist pastor who moved publicly egalitarian and clashed with the SBC Conservative Resurgence.

Aimee Byrd is the cleanest 'drift' case: Reformed (OPC) podcast personality whose 2020 book moved her from quiet complementarianism into the CBE orbit, prompting OPC discipline disputes. She remains formally Reformed but is now CBE-aligned in publication and speaking circuits.
notes: Collected from cbeinternational.org primary pages (2026-04-28 fetch) plus three Wayback Machine snapshots (2022-10, 2023-09, 2024-10) for historical board and staff rosters. Award rosters cover 2005-2024 (Lifetime Achievement), 2007-2024 (Micah), and 1989-2019 (Priscilla and Aquila). Dataset emphasizes verified, named individuals from official CBE pages; broader CBE-aligned figures (Beth Allison Barr, Aimee Byrd, Christa McKirland, Lucy Peppiatt, William Witt, Sarah Sumner) are included with a clearly marked 'endorser' classification because their books and public alignment with CBE are well-documented even when they do not appear on formal CBE rosters. CBE's 'Mutuality Matters' partner list and chapter-leader list were not fully available on public-facing pages at fetch time and are not enumerated here. Total verified entries: ~165.
